Definition: from G1256; a (mode of) discourse, i.e. "dialect":--language, tongue.
BiblicalUsage: A tongue is the language a people speaks, and at Pentecost the word does its great work. The crowd hears the apostles speak in their own tongue, Paul addresses the Jerusalem crowd in the Hebrew tongue, and the voice from heaven speaks to him in the same tongue on the Damascus road.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God speaks every tongue because He made them all. At Pentecost the gospel crossed the language barrier in a single morning, and it has been crossing it ever since.
RelatedTopics: Language; Mission; Outpouring of the Spirit
